# NotebookLM MCP + HTTP REST API

> Automate Google Gemini Notebook, formerly and still widely known as NotebookLM, at scale. Production-grade REST API and MCP server with citation-backed Q&A, full Studio content generation (audio, video, infographic, report, presentation, data table), multi-account rotation with auto-reauth, and 57 documented HTTP endpoints. Built for researchers, automators, and AI agents.

This is the canonical entry point for LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini) discovering this project. The library exposes Google NotebookLM via three surfaces — a local HTTP REST API (port 3000 by default) for n8n / Zapier / Make / curl integrations, an MCP server for Claude Code / Cursor / Codex agents, and a UTCP tool manual for clients that call the REST API natively. All share the same backend.

**Naming.** Google renamed NotebookLM to **Gemini Notebook** in July 2026. It is the same product, existing links redirect, and this project drives the same underlying service — the browser path was updated for the new interface in v2.3.0 and the internal RPC path in v3.0.0. The package and repository keep the `notebooklm` name, so both names refer to the same thing throughout this document.

The package is published to npm as `@roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp` (current version 4.8.0, Node 22 or newer). The maintained repository lives at https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp.

Two transports reach NotebookLM: its internal `batchexecute` RPC API first (10-100x faster than scraping and unaffected by interface rebrands), with a Playwright browser as an automatic fallback. Both ship permanently.

The HTTP API listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Exposing it to other machines requires `NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY`; without one the server refuses to start on a wider address. Browser callers must be allow-listed via `NOTEBOOKLM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

## Quick install

```bash
npx @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp@latest                               # MCP server (stdio)
npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth      # one-time Google login
```

For the REST API, clone and run the HTTP wrapper:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp.git
cd notebooklm-mcp && npm install && npm run build
npm run start:http         # REST API on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

## REST API at a glance

Single-call ask example, returns answer plus structured citations:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/ask \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "question": "Summarize chapter 3",
    "notebook_id": "your-notebook-id",
    "source_format": "json"
  }'
```

Response shape:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "status": "success",
    "question": "Summarize chapter 3",
    "answer": "Chapter 3 covers …",
    "session_id": "...",
    "sources": {
      "format": "json",
      "citations": [{ "marker": "[1]", "number": 1, "sourceText": "..." }],
      "extraction_success": true
    }
  }
}
```

## UTCP interface

[UTCP](https://www.utcp.io/), the Universal Tool Calling Protocol, is the inverse of MCP: there is no protocol server and no wrapper process. A client reads a tool manual once, then calls this REST API directly.

`GET /utcp` on a running server returns that manual, with every call address rebased on the address the request arrived at. The same document is published statically at https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json for a client configured before the server is up.

It declares 56 tools, named exactly as the MCP tools are, so `search_passages` is `search_passages` on both sides rather than something synthesised from a URL path. Every operation in the OpenAPI specification carries a matching `operationId`, so a client pointed straight at the specification converts it correctly on its own. Authentication is declared as an `api_key` in the `X-API-Key` header, which the server accepts alongside the bearer form; the key itself is never in the manual, only the literal `${NOTEBOOKLM_API_KEY}`, which is how a UTCP client asks for a value from its own environment.

## Rust client

A typed async Rust client is published from the same repository as the crate `notebooklm` (https://crates.io/crates/notebooklm, documentation at https://docs.rs/notebooklm). It covers all 56 operations, generated from the OpenAPI specification, with a synchronous twin behind a feature flag. It does not drive a browser itself: the Google session is bound to the machine it was created on, expires server-side while local cookies still look valid, and needs a patched driver, so the crate talks to the local server that already handles all three. Source: crates/notebooklm-client in https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp

## Ruby client

A Ruby client is published from the same repository as the gem `notebooklm` (https://rubygems.org/gems/notebooklm). It covers the same 56 operations, generated from the same specification, with every response shape documented field by field and no runtime dependencies — Net::HTTP and JSON only. Parameters are keyword arguments under the names the specification gives them; an absent value reads as nil rather than as zero or an empty string. Like the Rust crate it owns no browser and talks to the local server. Source: gems/notebooklm in https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp

- [Overview](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/)

- [REST API reference](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-rest-api): all 57 HTTP endpoints with request and response schemas.
- [Run 1 000 questions overnight](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/batch-1000-questions): production batch pattern, JSONL output, resume on restart.
- [n8n integration](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-n8n): HTTP Request node setup, scheduled queries, Slack flows.
- [Notebook library](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/NOTEBOOK-LIBRARY): multi-notebook management, search, scrape, bulk delete.
- [Auto-discovery](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/AUTO-DISCOVERY): autonomous metadata generation via NotebookLM queries.
- [Content management](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/CONTENT-MANAGEMENT): sources, audio, video, infographic, report, presentation, data table generation.
- [Multi-account](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-multi-account): account rotation, auto-reauth with TOTP support.
- [Docker](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/DOCKER): containerized deployment with noVNC, Synology / QNAP NAS support.
- [WSL usage](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/WSL-USAGE): running on Windows Subsystem for Linux.
- [Multi-interface](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/MULTI-INTERFACE): Claude Desktop and HTTP API simultaneously.
- [Troubleshooting](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/TROUBLESHOOTING): common issues and solutions.
- [Securing the HTTP API](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/security): bind address, bearer token, allowed origins, Docker requirements, vulnerability reporting.
- [Migrating from PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/compare): that project was archived in September 2026; 17 of its 19 tool names work here unchanged, and this page maps the rest.
- [Changelog](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/changelog): release history.

## Blog

Field notes on automating NotebookLM. Each post answers one question people
actually ask, states its limits, and names alternatives fairly.

- [Does NotebookLM have an API?](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/does-notebooklm-have-an-api): Google ships a Gemini Notebook Enterprise API in preview — the package `google.cloud.notebooklm.v1alpha` holds five services (notebooks, sources, labels, source discovery, one audio overview per notebook) and **no method that asks a notebook a question**, so no chat, no citation and no Studio output beyond audio; it needs a licensed user's OAuth token, reportedly $9 per licence per month with a 15-licence minimum. The consumer product has no developer key, authenticates with a machine-bound Google session, and the Podcast API is deprecated.
- [How to use NotebookLM from Claude Code](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-from-claude-code): install, the separate Google login, and why it must run in a terminal.
- [NotebookLM usage limits changed](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-usage-limits-automation): compute-based since 2 September 2026, refreshed every 5 hours, no daily count to plan against.
- [PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp is archived](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-mcp-archived-alternative): the alternatives, what moves on migration, and the environment variable that means two different things.
- [Getting NotebookLM citations as structured JSON](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-citations-as-json): source names versus cited excerpts, and why one costs more than the other.
- [Generating audio overviews programmatically](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-audio-overviews-programmatically): the official enterprise route, browser automation, and the internal interface.
- [NotebookLM in n8n, Zapier and Make](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-n8n-zapier-make): no connector exists; the local HTTP endpoint workaround and where it must run.
- [Running across multiple Google accounts](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-multiple-google-accounts): rotation multiplies a compute budget, not a quota; where sessions live and why they do not travel.
- [Your MCP server is probably listening on 0.0.0.0](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/mcp-server-listening-on-0-0-0-0): our own advisory, why loopback alone is not enough, and the three controls.
- [Calling NotebookLM from a UTCP client](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-utcp): UTCP is the inverse of MCP — no protocol server; the manual, the client code, and why an OpenAPI operation without an `operationId` silently disappears.
- [NotebookLM from Rust: a client that compiles](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-rust): why no Rust crate exists for the consumer product, a typed client over the local REST API, and the UTCP route that needs no types.
- [NotebookLM from Ruby](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-ruby): the gem, what a generated client gets right that a hand-written one does not, and how to generate one for any language from the specification.
- [Generate a NotebookLM client for any language in ten seconds](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-client-any-language): the published OpenAPI 3.1 specification, one openapi-generator command measured across Python, Go and Ruby, what a generated client gets and what it does not, and the four properties a specification needs to be generatable.
- [Gemini Notebook MCP servers compared](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/gemini-notebook-mcp-servers-compared): four live MCP servers measured the same day — stars, monthly installs from PyPI and npm, language, what each is shaped for, and where this one loses (228 stars against 20 151, 5 411 installs against 134 206). Includes the commands to retake every measurement.
- [Using NotebookLM from Python](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-python): no official SDK; the local REST endpoint, citations as JSON, retrieval that spends nothing, and overnight batching.
- [A literature review an agent can actually run](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/notebooklm-literature-review-agent): the four-step MCP loop — survey, retrieve, ask, store — and the habits that keep a long review inside the compute allowance.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp): source code, issues, releases.
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp): install via `npm install @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp` or `npx`.
- [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/openapi.yaml): importable in Postman / Insomnia / Bruno / Swagger UI.
- [UTCP manual](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/utcp.json): 56 named tools, for a Universal Tool Calling Protocol client that calls the REST API natively.
- [AI catalog](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json): the machine-readable index of what this domain publishes — the MCP server's registry manifest and the Claude Code skill — in the AI Catalog format that SEP-2127 points domain-level discovery at.
